items.title: Cổ phiếu công nghệ Mỹ biến động trước lo ngại về quy định AI | NHK WORLD-JAPAN News
items.summary:
Chiến thắng áp đảo của đảng Dn chủ trong cuộc bầu cử giữa kỳ của Mỹ đã làm dấy lên lo ngại về triển vọng của ngành trí tuệ nhn tạo và bán dẫn. Điều này khiến cổ phiếu công nghệ cao của Mỹ biến động.  
   
Đảng Dn chủ đã giành lại quyền kiểm soát cả hai viện Quốc hội trong cuộc bầu cử tuần trước. Các ứng viên đảng Dn chủ cũng chiến thắng trong các cuộc bầu cử thống đốc ở nhiều bang, trong đó có Texas, nơi có nhiều trung tm dữ liệu. [...] Một số nhà đầu tư lo ngại những chiến thắng này có thể dẫn đến việc siết chặt quy định đối với AI và các trung tm dữ liệu.  
   
Mối lo này đã gy ra làn sóng bán tháo cổ phiếu bán dẫn và các cổ phiếu khác liên quan đến AI. Hôm thứ Năm, chỉ số Nasdaq gồm nhiều cổ phiếu công nghệ ở New York giảm hơn 5%. Cổ phiếu công nghệ đã phần nào khôi phục vào ngày hôm sau nhưng các nhà đầu tư vẫn thận trọng. [...] Một số chuyên gia cho rằng các công ty trung tm dữ liệu mới nổi có thể gặp khó khăn về vốn nếu các quy định chặt chẽ hơn làm chậm tiến độ các dự án xy dựng mới. Các công ty này đã dựa vào khoản vay để mở rộng kinh doanh.  
   
Nguồn tin thị trường cho biết điều đó có nghĩa là cổ phiếu công nghệ có thể vẫn bất ổn trong thời gian trước mắt.

Công nghệTin tức công nghệ [...] ẢNH: APPLE

Chuyên gia Mark Gurman của Bloomberg cho biết trong bản tin Power On mới nhất rằng quy trình phát triển hệ điều hành của Apple thường được chia thành ba giai đoạn: M1, M2 và M3, mỗi giai đoạn kéo dài 8 tuần. Trong đó, 4 tuần đầu tiên dành cho việc lập trình các tính năng mới, 4 tuần tiếp theo để tích hợp chúng vào hệ điều hành.

args.text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ là:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

**Giải thích:**
Theo công thức nguyên hàm cơ bản của hàm số lũy thừa:
$$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \quad (với \; n \neq -1)$$

Áp dụng với $n = 2$:
$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

*(trong đó $C$ là hằng số tùy ý)*

results.title: AI Research Workflow Policy
results.facts: - Do not present a claim as verified unless it is supported by a primary source or reputable reporting. - For briefings, keep source URLs attached to each factual claim. - If sources conflict, state the conflict instead of forcing one conclusion.

items.summary:
# Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence

Intelligence in machines

"AI" redirects here. For other uses, see [AI (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_(disambiguation) "AI (disambiguation)") and [Artificial intelligence (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_(disambiguation) "Artificial intelligence (disambiguation)").

**Artificial intelligence** ( **AI**) is the capability of [computational systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer "Computer") to perform tasks typically associated with [human intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_intelligence "Human intelligence"), such as [learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning "Learning"), [reasoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reason "Reason"), [problem-solving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem-solving "Problem-solving"), [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception "Perception"), and [decision-making](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision-making "Decision-making"). It is also a field of research spanning [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"), [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering "Engineering"), and [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") that develops and studies methods and [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software "Software") enabling machines to perceive their environment and use [learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") and [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence "Intelligence") to take actions that maximise their chances of achieving defined goals.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211%E2%80%934-1)

Prominent [applications of AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applications_of_artificial_intelligence "Applications of artificial intelligence") include advanced [web search engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_search_engine "Web search engine"), [chatbots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot "Chatbot"), [virtual assistants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_assistant "Virtual assistant"), [autonomous vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_vehicles "Autonomous vehicles"), play and analysis in [strategy games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_game "Strategy game") (e.g., [chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess "Chess") and [Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(game) "Go (game)")), and [content generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") (e.g., text, images, audio, and videos).

The traditional goals of AI research include learning, [reasoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_reasoning "Automated reasoning"), [knowledge representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_representation "Knowledge representation"), [planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_planning_and_scheduling "Automated planning and scheduling"), [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing"), and [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_perception "Machine perception"), as well as support for [robotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotics "Robotics").[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Problems_of_AI-2) To reach these goals, AI researchers use techniques including [state space search](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search "State space search") and [mathematical optimisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_optimization "Mathematical optimization"), [formal logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_logic "Formal logic"), [artificial neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning) "Neural network (machine learning)"), and methods based on [statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistics "Statistics"), [operations research](https://en.wikipedia

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary: Goldberg, who was recently inducted into the National Academy of Engineering, is presenting the new approach and results from months of testing this week at the Conference on Robot Learning. He and his team are also releasing open-source code for other roboticists to experiment with, built on NVIDIA’s Isaac open simulation framework  for developers, as well as an industry-standard benchmark for evaluating the performance of robots across industrial tasks. [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: Kenwood High School JROTC Robotics Program earns regional recognition - ClarksvilleNow.com
items.summary: During the current robotics’ competition season, Team 26163X captured first place at the Tennessee State Fair Robotics Competition. The team followed that performance with another first-place finish at a competition in Elizabethton, Tennessee, where it also received a technical award recognizing excellence in robot design and engineering. [...] The teams are scheduled to compete in the V5RC Arsenal Tech Fall Tournament in Fort Wayne, Indiana, and later at the Louisville Slugger Signature Competition, an event expected to attract top robotics programs from across the United States and several international teams. Cadets involved in the program say the experience extends beyond competition. “Robotics has taught us how to work together under pressure and find solutions when things don’t go as planned,” said a member of Team 26163X.”Every [...] CLARKSVILLE TN – The Kenwood High School JROTC Robotics Program has grown from a single robotics team into a four-team program that is competing successfully at regional and national-level events. The program currently fields Teams 26163X, 26163A, 26163L, and 26163S, providing students with opportunities to develop skills in engineering, programming, and problem-solving.
